skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation).

skills.name: skill-picker
skills.description: Use whenever the user has a task and wants to know which installed skill applies, or says "which skill", "what skill should I use", "pick a skill", "route this", or hands you a task without naming a skill. The picker reads the task, matches it against the 60 installed skills (including optimization, code simplification, and project debloat skills), and returns the single best skill plus a one-line why, the exact invocation, and any overlap or gap. Trigger this before starting any task whose domain matches an installed skill — do not default to doing the work yourself when a dedicated skill exists.

skills.name: thinking-first-principles
skills.description: When a constraint is treated as fixed, separate physics from convention, keep only independently supported primitives, and rebuild the simplest solution that satisfies real constraints.

skills.name: thinking-margin-of-safety
skills.description: When provisioning, setting a limit, or committing an estimate under uncertainty, size a buffer to residual error and the cost of breach—not to the optimistic edge.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
